# There Is Absolutely Nothing New in the Pragmatic Method

There is absolutely nothing new in the pragmatic method,[^1] a method of settling metaphysical disputes that otherwise might be interminable.[^2] Socrates was an adept at it.[^3] Aristotle used it methodically.[^4] Locke, Berkeley and Hume made momentous contributions to truth by its means.[^5] Shadworth Hodgson keeps insisting that realities are only what they are 'known-as.'[^6] But these forerunners of pragmatism used it in fragments: they were preluders only.[^7] Not until in our time has it generalized itself, become conscious of a universal mission, pretended to a conquering destiny.[^8]
